summary.intent: Decide whether Phase 72 needed discussion before planning, audit pending todos for drift from Phases 70/70.1/71, then plan/execute/ship Phase 72 — but this was interrupted by newly-discovered CI regressions (web-e2e and desktop-e2e failing on main), which became the priority: diagnose and fix all regressions plus resulting web-e2e flakiness across PRs #600 and #601.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and updated ROADMAP source lists for Phase 72/73 (stashed, uncommitted per user instruction). Found and fixed three real CI regressions traced to Phase 70.1/71: a stale rotation-durability test helper, a FUSE seq-1/anti-equivocation collision, and a flaky sdk-e2e idempotency assertion — plus a Greptile-flagged perf nit. PR #601 (FUSE fix) merged and validated green on all 3 desktop OSes. PR #600 accumulated the web/test fixes plus 4 additional web-e2e timing-flake fixes (4.10, 4.11, 6.6.2, 8.2) discovered via extensive local reproduction, verified green under a CI-equivalent timeout regime, and committed — with pushing, final rerun, merge, and resuming Phase 72 planning left as the immediate next step.

repo: GSD todos are closed by deletion from pending/ into completed/, not into a resolved/ folder (which is empty/unused) — check completed/ for retired todos.

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers only on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PR authors must manually dispatch against their branch (`gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>`, not `-f ref=`) to get real e2e signal before merging.
ci.yml runs sdk-e2e on pull_request, so sdk-e2e failures do show up on PRs directly.

Playwright's `ciFloor()` helper only raises wait timeouts (e.g. 15s→60s) under `process.env.CI` — local runs use much tighter timeouts, so local flakes at 15-30s boundaries are often not real CI flakes, just local/CI timeout asymmetry.

playwright.config.ts webServer blocks use `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally to mirror CI's timeout floor fights an already-running dev stack unless reuse is temporarily patched.

Phase 71 (#599) renamed share DTO fields (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName) but left tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/*.mts drivers using the old field names, causing API 400s via forbidNonWhitelisted.

Phase 70.1 collapsed two IndexedDB stores (generation-high-water, seq-high-water) into one `rotation-floor` store (DB cipherbox-rotation-state v2, keyed by nodeId) but didn't update the web-e2e test helper reading the old store names.
Repo philosophy is retries:0 / fix-flakiness-at-source — confirmed by user decision not to add CI retries even after multiple flaky tests surfaced.

Phase 71 shipped (#599) without retiring any of its 8 source todos from pending/, and left three pieces of test/fixture drift unaddressed (stale .mts DTO fields, an assertion that didn't account for its own idempotency, and exposing a FUSE bug) — a pattern worth checking after future phase ships.

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish without resolving IPNS first; fixed to resolve via resolve_ipns_for_replay and route Found→CAS retry, NotFound→true first-publish, Error→hard fail.

publish_with_cas_retry took an optional preresolved_seq param (Greptile perf fix) to skip a redundant second sequence resolve on the Found path; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after conflict.
readDurableFloors/writeDurableSeqFloor pointed at retired IndexedDB store names; fixed to use the collapsed rotation-floor store with read-modify-write semantics.
POST /shares body and received-share reads used pre-#599 DTO field names; local vars named rootIpnsName from the vault endpoint (lines 245/273/468) are unrelated and were correctly left unchanged.

Test 21 (D-06) asserted exactly one-200-one-409 for concurrent first-publish, but Phase 71's same-CID idempotency legitimately allows two 200s; rewritten to accept both outcomes while still rejecting 5xx/multiple-409.

6.6.2's getVersionCount()===1 gate was a no-op (restore swaps current↔v1, count is 1 both before and after) providing zero wait for IPNS republish; replaced with expect.poll reading actual editor content until it matches expected post-restore text.

8.2 deletes 3 files serially, each IPNS-gated; had no test.setTimeout override so ran under default 90s budget and cumulatively overflowed even though each delete succeeded — fixed with test.setTimeout(150000).
4.10 batch delete's waitForItemToDisappear used a bare 15s local timeout (60s under CI via ciFloor); genuinely needed >15s on this hardware (passed at 29.3s after bump to 30s).

Recipient-side (Bob) shared-mkdir appear-waits used bare timeout:30000 while the owner-side wait at line 555 already used 60000 — shared-write is the highest-latency path yet got half the budget; bumped both recipient waits to 60000.

workflow: When a background/local test run cascades on an unrelated early failure, blocking downstream target tests from executing, re-running repeatedly on a 'warm stack' doesn't reliably converge — different ambient IPNS-timing flakes surface each pass; running once under the CI-equivalent timeout regime is more efficient than iterating locally.

For local verification of CI-gated flaky tests, temporarily patching config to mirror CI's exact timeout regime (and reverting after) is a valid way to get a representative pass before committing, rather than chasing individual local-only timeout artifacts.

When a PR accumulates multiple unrelated fixes (test regression + CodeRabbit nit + flaky-test hardening + timing fixes), keep updating the PR description to reflect the full commit set so reviewers aren't surprised.

GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch inputs can silently reject `-f ref=` with 422 if the workflow file on the target ref predates that input name — use `--ref <branch>` to dispatch from the branch's own definition instead.

Sequencing CI regression fixes: cheap/low-risk fixes should be verified and merged first (desktop #601) before folding in a second wave of harder-to-reproduce flakiness fixes (web #600), rather than blocking everything on the hardest problem.

friction: Local web-e2e verification required 7+ sequential full-workflow runs (~10+ min each) because different ambient IPNS-timing flakes (4.10, then 4.11, then 2.1) kept cascading and blocking the actual target tests (6.6.2, 8.2) from ever executing.
CI=1 locally conflicted with webServer.reuseExistingServer (!process.env.CI), requiring a temporary config patch to test under CI's real 60s timeout floor.
Initially checked the wrong todo directory (resolved/, which was empty) before being corrected to completed/.
gh workflow run with -f ref= returned HTTP 422 because main's workflow definition predated that input; had to use --ref instead.
e2e workflows (ci-e2e.yml) don't run on PRs at all, forcing manual workflow_dispatch against branches to get real pre-merge validation — a recurring extra step for every fix.

Phase 72 planning was interrupted mid-CONTEXT.md-authoring by the CI fire, requiring a stash of in-progress ROADMAP/todo changes and a branch switch back to main — added bookkeeping overhead to resume later.
PR #601's sdk-e2e failure required distinguishing whether it was the same Test 21 flake (fix living on #600, not yet on #601) versus a new issue — added a wait-and-confirm step before proceeding.
